The end of the Great Wall depends on which section and historical framing you use. Most sources agree the eastern end is at Shanhai Pass (Laolongtou), where the wall meets the Bohai Sea near Qinhuangdao [d2,d3,d5,d6]. In contrast, the western end is widely cited as Jiayu Pass (or Jiayuguan) in Gansu province [d4,d6,d8]. Some Ming-era mappings place the eastern terminus farther northeast at Hushan on the Manchu/Korean border [d7].

[d2] and [d6] describe Laolongtou at Shanhai Pass as the seaward end; [d4], [d6], and [d8] identify Jiayu Pass/Jiayuguan as the western end; [d7] adds the Hushan endpoint for the Ming Great Wall’s full extent.
